body: I wasn't immediately able to reproduce (Ubuntu, 3.10.2-rc1). I'll try this again later today.

Few more observations:

- it does behave the same for me on macOS with 3.10.0ish, 3.10.1, 3.10.2-rc1
- additionally, it occurs also when more than one PartConv is started within a parallel group, _regardless of timing_, if
  - using built-in input/output on the macbook pro
  - not specifying hardware buffer size
- I tested on Ubuntu, and the error indeed did not occur

To clarify the second point - it works (and breaks) as described in the PR, with the exception of using built-in in/out _and_ not specifying hardware buffer size, when it breaks regardless of the  `syncBetweenSynths` flag (outputs loud noise). ~~Maybe there is some kind of weird interaction between memory allocation and the PortAudio backend?~~

Edit: 
I tested this also with supernova built with native JACK backend (on macOS, with jackosx), and it also breaks (regardless of timing). In that case I guess this is not related to the PortAudio backend.

body:
What are the async things that should happen before sync?
I suppose that SynthDef sending only?

@sonoro1234 
Do you mean in the reproducer for the bug?
Then it think the following should happen before the sync:
- ~~sending a synthdef~~ 
- allocating playbuf and partconv buffers
- starting pargroup

But the sync triggered by `~syncBetweenSynths` only waits for sending the synthdef and nothing else as the other async tasks already have a sync afterwards.
It is strange that only synthdef sending causes this!

@dyfer
I could not find sync related actions on PartConv. There is no LOCK_SNDBUF_SHARED which could create problems between threads.
I remember that I did a correction on PartConv https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/pull/2015
It is a complicated UGen and I did a rework for not needing the preparation phase which I am using in my personal work with supernova and dont show any problem. It is here https://github.com/sonoro1234/DWGReverb/blob/master/PartitionedConvolutionTrig.cpp, snappiz did the sclang part. Perhaps you could give it a try?
The whole repo is https://github.com/sonoro1234/DWGReverb

by the way, I could not find the meaning of `(1, 0.99998 .. 0)` What is it doing?

@sonoro1234 I made some tests and it looks like FFT processing in general is affected, not only PartConv.

Could you confirm whether this happens on your machine? (the code in the first post is updated accordingly)

> by the way, I could not find the meaning of (1, 0.99998 .. 0) What is it doing?

This is another way of creating arithmetic series. Syntax is a little different than `Array.series` - it is `(first, second .. last)`.
```SuperCollider
(1, 0.99998 .. 0);
-> [ 1.0, 0.99998, 0.99996, 0.99994, 0.99992, 0.9999, 0.99988, 0.99986, 0.99984, 0.99982, 0.9998, 0.99978, 0.99976, 0.99974, 0.99972, 0.9997, 0.99968, 0.99966, 0.99964, 0.99962, 0.9996, 0.99958, 0.99956, 0.99954, 0.99952, 0.9995, 0.99948, 0.99946, 0.99944, 0.99942, 0.9994, 0.99938, 0.99936, 0.99934, 0.99932, 0.9993, 0.99928, 0.99926, 0.99924, 0.99922, 0.9992, 0.99918, 0.99916, 0.99914, 0.99912, 0.9991, 0.99908, 0.99906, 0.99904, 0.99902, 0.999, 0.99898, 0.99896, 0.99894, 0.99892, 0.9989, 0.99888, 0.99886, 0.99...etc...

(1, 0.99998 .. 0).size;
-> 50000
```

I haven't had a chance to test your convolver, sorry.

SC win32 mingw compiled:
I have done the test. There is a variation in volume in each execution (with or without  ~syncBetweenSynths) caused by f.coin and 0.5.coin that makes difficult to make conclusions.
It seems to be a variation in stereo between  ~syncBetweenSynths false and true
The test with scsynth performs similar to supernova.
I still dont understand what sync is doing there as there is no async action involved.

@sonoro1234 I'm very sorry! I The top example was not updated. I updated it now. (I must've been in the preview mode previously...)

The issue seems to be with FFT processing in general, not only PartConv.
~syncBetweenSynths makes no difference for me on SC win32 mingw compiled with the updated example

Further investigation - this might be a lead (see [source](https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/common/SC_fftlib.cpp#L23)):
> vDSP uses a "SplitBuf" as an intermediate representation of the data.
For speed we keep this global, although this makes the code non-thread-safe.

Is the global `splitBuf` the culprit then? How would we address this maintaining performance?

For supernova, do we know if vDSP is used? I see this kind of thing:

https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/common/SC_fftlib.cpp#L360 <https://github.com/supercollider/supercollider/blob/develop/common/SC_fftlib.cpp#L360>
